key_insight: Providers generally accepted the AI CDSS in eSanjeevani, but acceptance dropped when the system’s suggestions were absent, inaccurate, or poorly calibrated to the case.
clinical_relevance: For telemedicine teams, AI decision support appears most useful when it is reliable, clearly presented, and aligned with clinicians’ workflow and judgment.
method: Program feedback web survey of hub clinicians and spoke providers in eSanjeevani
Analyzed role-specific experience with symptom summaries, AI differential diagnoses, and symptom capture tools
Compared acceptance patterns within roles using absolute differences with Newcombe 95% CIs; open comments were content-analyzed
evidence_signal: The survey included 190 hub and 662 spoke respondents from 13 and 15 states, and most rated the tools positively, though experience varied by whether AI suggestions matched clinician impressions.
watch_item: Reported acceptance was high, but technical gaps, missing suggestions, and mixed question volume suggest implementation quality may strongly affect real-world uptake.
paper_title: Provider Experiences with AI Clinical Decision Support in eSanjeevani
